evidence_claims.claim_text: On 2026-07-23, Tinder said Events was live in Los Angeles and nine additional cities: New York City, Dallas, Denver, Kansas City, Phoenix, Berlin, Munich, Zurich and Geneva; 26 cities by the end of September remained a forward plan.

Tinder's internal Los Angeles pilot data reported engagement by 66% of eligible Photo Verified active users, including 71% of users aged 18-24 and 63% of users aged 25+, with 53% week-over-week return to the Events tab; Tinder stated that these figures may not represent other markets.
Tinder reported that one 60-person candlelight ceramics class sold out within one day of partner promotion; this is a single-event company-reported result, not evidence of market-wide sell-through.

On Match Group's second-quarter earnings call, CEO Spencer Rascoff described Events as scaling through a low-cost model built primarily on event-provider partnerships and set a 75-city year-end target; the cost characterization and target were management statements rather than disclosed Event-level unit economics.

TechCrunch reported that Tinder revenue declined in 2026 Q2 and monthly active users were down 7% year over year; these platform-wide figures are economic context and do not establish any effect of Events.

chip_support.reason: The Los Angeles engagement and return figures are direct demand signals but are internal, cohort-limited and not independently verified.
A 60-person class reportedly sold out in one day, but the signal is limited to one company-reported event.

unresolved: No independently measured Events attendance, conversion, retention or ticket-sales series was found; press coverage repeats company metrics and does not convert them into verified adoption.
No Events-specific revenue, cost, partner-economics or causal impact on Tinder user or revenue trends was disclosed.
Investor-facing attention is evidenced by earnings-call discussion, but no Event-specific investor allocation or external investment was identified.
The 26-city and 75-city figures are targets beyond the ten cities confirmed live in the dated launch evidence; no dated Korean availability or adoption evidence was found.

evidence_claims.claim_text: Caelith AI announced Fypro's public launch on 2026-06-25 as a creator stack that analyzes a social account, produces a content and monetization plan, builds a branded site and storefront, and creates an exportable customer list.
Fypro's public pricing page listed a free plan at $0 per month, Pro at $29 per month and Max at $200 per month, with card rates starting at 2.8% plus $0.30 for Pro and 2.6% plus $0.30 for Max.

Fypro's site invited visitors to join more than 2,000 creators already running Fypro and said its model was refined by more than 2,000 creators; no public methodology, paid-user split, cohort date or retention series accompanied the count.

Product Hunt displayed Fypro with 592 points and ranked it number 2 of the day and number 3 of the week for 2026-07-02; this verifies launch-platform attention, not creator adoption or investor funding.

chip_support.reason: Product Hunt's recorded points and day/week ranks are direct platform-attention evidence, scoped to the launch community.

unresolved: No public Fypro or Caelith AI funding round, named investor or other investor-attention event was verified.
No independently measured active-creator count was found; Product Hunt and editorial coverage repeat company-supplied creator and output figures.

No paid-customer count, subscription mix, revenue, GMV, creator earnings distribution, retention or cohort economics was disclosed, so the visible pricing surface does not establish economic durability.
No dated evidence established creator geography or Korean adoption, and no causal effect on creator revenue or audience growth was verified.

evidence_claims.claim_text: Frido's official Experience Store locator displayed city filters for Pune, Bangalore, Hyderabad, Gurugram, Mumbai, Delhi and Faridabad and stated that stores offer walk-ins, product trials, free consultations, 3D foot scans, gait analysis and personalized recommendations.

Indiaretailing reported on 2026-06-16 that Frido had launched 15 company-owned, company-operated experiential stores across Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Pune; about 70% were in malls, and formats ranged from 250 to 1,900 square feet.
Frido told Indiaretailing that it planned 70 to 100 stores across India by FY28 and 350 to 400 jobs; these are future targets rather than completed expansion or verified demand.

CB Insights records a $1.52 million private-equity round for Frido on 2023-03-29 from BL Taparia Family Office, Chona Family Office and MGA Ventures; this investor attention predates the 2026 store rollout and does not evidence current store performance.

chip_support.reason: The official store surface explicitly offers scans, gait analysis and personalized recommendations tied to an individual's feet and comfort needs.

unresolved: No independently measured store footfall, transactions, conversion, repeat purchase, scan usage or customer retention was found, so verified adoption remains unresolved.
No store-level revenue, contribution margin, payback period, lease burden or profitability evidence was found; rollout scale and a historic funding round do not establish economic durability.
The official locator repeated identical rating text across store cards and showed at least one city/address mismatch, so those ratings were not treated as adoption evidence.
No dated Korean store availability, customer adoption or causal spillover evidence was found.
